title: Payments & Cashless Living
blurb: How I talk about money moving without cash — the rails, the fees, and who actually pays them.

entries.gloss: The fee a merchant's bank pays the cardholder's bank on every card transaction.
entries.context: In card-network talk it is scheme-set and mostly invisible to shoppers; in UPI discourse 'zero MDR' made the whole fee question a policy flashpoint.
entries.usage: Explain how interchange differs from MDR, and who actually ends up paying it.

entries.gloss: India's instant bank-to-bank payment rail, run as a public infrastructure layer.
entries.context: In product talk it is a checkout button; in policy talk it is a public-goods argument about pricing and market power.
entries.usage: Compare paying with UPI versus a card network, in terms of cost and data trails.

entries.gloss: A standing instruction that lets someone debit your account on a schedule or trigger.
entries.context: In everyday banking it is an auto-pay you approve once; in lending it becomes the collection mechanism that decides default behavior.
entries.usage: Walk through what happens when a subscription mandate fails and how retries work.

entries.gloss: The process that moves actual money between banks after customers' transactions clear.
entries.context: In commerce dashboards 'settled' means money you can spend; in clearing-system talk it is the netting that happens at the central bank.
entries.usage: Explain why a sale today can settle two days later and what risk that gap creates.

entries.gloss: A forced reversal where the cardholder's bank pulls funds back from the merchant.
entries.context: In consumer talk it is fraud protection; in merchant talk it is a dispute cost with evidence deadlines and penalty fees.
entries.usage: Draft a friendly email asking a customer to contact their bank before filing a chargeback.

entries.gloss: The bank that gives you your card and is on the hook for paying merchants.
entries.context: In risk talk issuers approve or decline; in loyalty talk they own the rewards program that shapes how you swipe.
entries.usage: List what an issuer checks in the two seconds after a card is swiped.

entries.gloss: The bank or processor that collects card payments on behalf of a merchant.
entries.context: In onboarding it underwrites the merchant's risk; in fees talk it is the party that bundles interchange, scheme fees, and its own markup.
entries.usage: Explain why a small business might be rejected by an acquirer before opening.

entries.gloss: Replacing card details with a stand-in token so merchants never store the real number.
entries.context: In security talk it shrinks breach blast radius; in platform talk it is also a lock-in tool, since tokens often only work inside one ecosystem.
entries.usage: Explain how card tokenization changes what a hacker can steal from a merchant database.

entries.gloss: Know Your Customer — the identity checks required before financial accounts work fully.
entries.context: In compliance talk it is a legal floor; in inclusion talk it is the barrier that decides who can open an account at all.
entries.usage: Outline a KYC flow that stays compliant but takes under two minutes for a feature phone user.

entries.gloss: Merchant Discount Rate — the total fee a merchant pays on a transaction.
entries.context: In card payments it bundles interchange and processor fees; in UPI discourse zero-MDR made acceptance free and changed merchant behavior.
entries.usage: Break down a 2 percent MDR into its components and say who earns each part.
